subject: Argus4b elevated 5xx/timeouts — customer notice and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] Argus4b spike — 5xx/timeouts across us-west-2 pool

Team,

Monitoring alerted at 09:08 PDT: Argus4b serving pool in us-west-2 shows an abrupt jump in 5xx responses and streaming timeouts. Current symptoms: 5xx rate ~4.6% (baseline ~0.02%), median stream latency increased from 120ms to ~1.9s, and a subset of requests see 10s+ server-side timeouts.

Initial triage:
- Kernel/driver regressions: no recent infra kernel pushes to these nodes in the last 24h.
- Model variant change: no config flips; Argus4b builds in prod pinned to v20270430.
- KV cache hot-evictions observed for ~20% of requests.

Action taken so far:
- Autoscaling paused to avoid noisy instability.
- Routing rule applied to shift non-critical traffic to Argus4b-small fallback.
- Detailed logs exported to incident bucket; attaching early-summary to thread.

Marcus — looping you in for customer comms and SLA notification. Karthik/Neha, can you join triage and confirm whether this correlates to recent quantization kernel changes we tested last week?

Marissa
SRE — Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: argus4b_early_alert.json (logs referenced), quick_snapshot.png (error rate graph)

Subject: Argus4b — temporary elevated 5xx/timeouts (initial notice)

Jane,

Wanted to let you know we detected an elevated 5xx and timeout rate affecting calls served by Argus4b in the us-west-2 region starting ~09:06 PDT this morning. We've routed non-critical traffic to a fallback model and are actively triaging the root cause. Immediate customer impact: up to ~3% of requests for some of your batch endpoints may have returned 5xx or timed out; streaming workloads saw increased latency.

What we are doing:
- Our SREs are investigating kernel/serving runtime regressions and KV cache eviction patterns.
- We’ve applied routing fallbacks to reduce exposure and paused non-essential autoscaling.
- We'll provide regular updates and a post-incident summary with timeline and mitigations.

No action required from your side at this point — we’ll follow up within the hour with findings and expected ETA for full recovery. Apologies for the disruption; we know this impacts production traffic.

Thanks,

Subject: Argus4b — incident summary, mitigation, and next steps (post-incident)

Hi Jane and ScaleFast team,

Thank you for your patience. Below is a concise post-incident update for the Argus4b elevated 5xx/timeouts observed on 2027-05-28. We’ve attached a short timeline and the raw error summary.

Summary of impact
- Window: 2027-05-28 09:06–13:23 PDT (us-west-2 traffic); customer-visible errors peaked between 09:10–10:05 PDT.
- Observed: increased 5xx rate (max 5.1%), elevated stream latencies, and intermittent server-side timeouts for requests >8s.
- ScaleFast impact: ~2.6% of your calls to generation endpoints returned 5xx or timed out during peak window. We did not detect permanent data loss; retries processed successfully after fallback routing for the majority of requests.

Root cause (short)
- A regression in a quantization-friendly kernel roll (internal CL #13489) caused degraded memory access patterns on Argus4b inference shards under specific sequence-length distributions. This manifested as KV-cache churn and downstream request stalls, producing timeouts and 5xx errors. The kernel was on a limited rollout group which unexpectedly overlapped with several us-west-2 nodes serving heavy sequence-length traffic.

Mitigations performed
- Immediate: Routed non-critical and batch traffic to Argus4b-small and the rw-fallback-model at 09:20 PDT; this reduced visible errors by ~60% by 09:40 PDT.
- Rollback: Removed the kernel change from affected nodes and re-deployed the previous stable kernel version (completed by 12:10 PDT).
- Stabilization: Gradual traffic re-introduction and KV cache warmup completed; by 13:23 PDT the error rate returned to baseline.

Customer impact notes and recommendations
- No confirmed data loss; most clients’ retries were successful. If you notice missing items, our logs include request IDs and timestamps — we can provide exports for reconciliation.
- For ingestion-heavy jobs, we recommend keeping a short retry window (exponential backoff) during full rollouts; we’ll notify customers earlier during future kernel rollouts.

Follow-ups and commitments
- Postmortem doc and timeline attached (argus4b_incident_timeline.pdf).
- We’ll update our kernel rollout checklist to include sequence-length sampling and isolation of rollout cohorts by model and region.
- Karthik and Neha will prepare a short runbook update and a plan to add a pre-rollout KV cache pressure test. Target delivery: 2027-06-11.

Attachments: argus4b_incident_timeline.pdf, argus4b_error_summary.csv, svc_logs_20270528.tar.gz

If you want a 30-minute sync to walk the timeline and reconciliation steps, we can schedule tomorrow morning. Again, apologies for the interruption — we’re updating our process to reduce the risk of recurrence.

Best,
Marcus Lin
